channel.title: LC Insight
channel.description: Read the chain, not the rumors. Crypto market news and on-chain analysis.

item.title: Whales and smart money put $3 million into ZAMA as it fell 14% in a week
item.description: ZAMA drew the heaviest combined buying in DeepSea's weekly data, with coins moving to cold storage. Two USD.AI tokens, CHIP and sUSDai, came next.

item.title: DeFi lenders supplied $12.7 billion in a week. Morpho Blue had 84% of liquidations
item.description: DeepSea's lending data for October 26 to November 1 shows deposits far ahead of withdrawals, borrowing almost exactly matched by repayments, and $12.69 million liquidated, most of it on Morpho Blue.

item.title: Whales cut $28.9 million of LBTC in a week. Smart money bought just $127,900
item.description: Lombard's bitcoin token on Ethereum was the most sold token in DeepSea's weekly data, by a wide margin. Whales also cut $6.47 million of ARB, with DeepSea flagging moves to cold storage.

item.title: PEPE and SHIB flowed into US and European exchanges as $120 million in bitcoin left
item.description: DeepSea's weekly data shows Western exchanges nearly flat overall, at minus $54.98 million. Under the surface, memecoins were deposited, bitcoin was withdrawn, Kraken lost 1,526 BTC and one $399.78 million USDC transfer left Coinbase.

item.title: 448 of 617 Solana influencers lost money last week. The best one won all seven days
item.description: DeepSea's tracked crypto influencers on Solana closed the week $395,600 down. A trader called zeropnl made $82,900 with seven green days, while one smart money wallet lost $1.81 million in a single day.

item.title: Hyperliquid's big traders bet $3.78 billion on a drop. One put $126 million on HYPE rising
item.description: DeepSea's tracked traders held six dollars of shorts for every dollar of longs last week. Against that tide, one wallet opened a $126.62 million HYPE long, and a 40x bitcoin bet sat 2.4% from liquidation.

item.title: $255 million in USDT left Asian exchanges in a week. Gold tokens, USDe and RLUSD moved in
item.description: DeepSea's weekly data shows Asian exchanges losing USDT and USDT0 while tokenized gold and smaller dollar tokens arrived. In the last 24 hours, one shark wallet traded $47.8 million of RLUSD on Ethereum.

item.title: Binance took in a net 66,386 bitcoin, worth $5.2 billion, in the week it was hacked
item.description: DeepSea's data shows a net $5.04 billion flowing into Binance from October 26 to November 1, almost all of Asia's net inflow. Who sent it? The data cannot say.

item.title: $307 million in hack-linked bitcoin hit exchanges in one week. OKX got the biggest share
item.description: DeepSea counted 680 deposits of tainted funds into exchanges from October 26 to November 1, nearly all in BTC. OKX took $139.96 million in just 55 of them, including a run of near-identical $15.47 million transfers.

item.title: A fake job interview opened the door to Binance's $6.34 billion hack, its own report says
item.description: Binance's first incident report traces the October 29 theft to a staged hiring process, a poisoned coding test and a developer tool swapped for malware. Then nine minutes of hot-wallet transfers did the rest.

item.title: 2026's biggest airdrops: $809 million claimed, 9 of 11 tokens below first close
item.description: On-chain data compiled by Bitquery puts 51 large EVM airdrops this year at $809.4 million and 2.02 million claiming wallets. Most claimers moved their tokens within a day, and CoinGecko prices show only Backpack and Espresso above their first daily close.

item.title: Backpack gave users 25% of BP and insiders nothing. BP is up 285% from its first close
item.description: Backpack airdropped 250 million BP to points holders and Mad Lads owners on March 23, 2026, worth about $57 million at CoinGecko's first daily close. No team or investor tokens unlocked, and the next 37.5% of supply unlocks only when the company hits growth milestones.

item.title: MegaETH's MEGA is down 73% since launch. Who really got the 15% 'community' share?
item.description: MegaETH launched MEGA on April 30, 2026, after hitting the first of four network milestones. At least a third of its 15% community allocation was sold at auction, MegaETH has not said how much was given away free, and 53% of supply still waits on future milestones.

item.title: 82,671 wallets claimed Brevis' BREV airdrop. 45% of the claim pot was never collected
item.description: Brevis opened its BREV claim on January 6, 2026, after a points campaign, a Kaito leaderboard and a Binance HODLer drop. The Ethereum claim contract still holds 45% of its 20 million BREV, and the token trades about 77% below its first daily close.

item.title: Jupuary 2026 never landed: 75% of JUP votes shelved a 700 million JUP airdrop
item.description: Jupiter's yearly airdrop was due to start with 200 million JUP in early 2026. Stakers voted on February 22 to park all 700 million tokens in a locked community wallet instead. No new vote has been called since, and JUP now trades about 41% above its close that day.

item.title: Polymarket has no POLY token. So why is it still pursuing a POLY trademark?
item.description: Polymarket's help center says it has announced no airdrop and no token launch, and that all rewards are paid in pUSD. Meanwhile a February application to trademark "POLY" for crypto token services is still alive, with a reply filed on November 2.

item.title: MetaMask's points season ended in LINEA allocations. It has "no plans" for a MASK token
item.description: MetaMask Rewards Season 1, from October 28, 2025, to January 23, 2026, gave users above 1,000 points a LINEA allocation. LINEA now trades about 28% below its price on February 23, when MetaMask said the claim window had closed, and the help center says there is no $MASK token plan and no next season, only short campaigns paid in mUSD.

item.title: What is a rug pull? How crypto exit scams work and 6 warning signs to check
item.description: A rug pull is when a project's own insiders take buyers' money and walk away, by draining the pool, printing tokens through a backdoor or dumping their supply. Most of the warning signs are public on-chain before you buy.

item.title: What is a gas fee? How Ethereum fees work, who gets paid and why they spike
item.description: A gas fee is what you pay Ethereum to run a transaction: gas used times the base fee plus an optional tip. The base fee is burned, the tip goes to the validator, and the price can climb 12.5% a block when the network gets busy.

item.title: Thailand crypto rules explained: licenses, the Bybit and OKX blocks, and tax
item.description: Any crypto exchange, broker or dealer serving people in Thailand needs a Thai SEC license, and since April 2025 offshore platforms with Thai features can be blocked. Bybit, OKX and three others were named for blocking from June 28, 2025. Here is what that means for users, payments and tax.

item.title: What is TON? Telegram's blockchain explained, and why Toncoin is now Gram
item.description: TON (The Open Network) is a proof-of-stake blockchain wired into Telegram, with a wallet built into the messenger. Its coin, long called Toncoin, now trades as Gram (GRAM), and that rename is the first thing a new user can trip over.

item.title: Compound's fourth retreat in a month: a vote to pull 90 ETH and 42,000 USDC off Unichain
item.description: A Compound DAO vote closing November 3, with no votes against so far, would send reserves from its deprecated Unichain markets back to Ethereum. A bigger 534,530 USDT withdrawal from Polygon was filed and canceled within an hour.

item.title: Polymarket adds 15-minute gold and silver bets. One early window traded just $100
item.description: Polymarket has added 15-minute and one-hour Up or Down markets on gold and silver, settled by Chainlink price streams. The format began with crypto, where Chainlink says it has passed $9 billion in volume, but the metal markets start almost empty.

item.title: What is Bitcoin? How it works, why only 21 million exist and the risks
item.description: Bitcoin is a digital currency that moves directly between users on a public network, with no bank or company in the middle. Miners secure it with computing power, its supply is capped at 21 million coins, and BTC traded near $77,323 as of November 2, 2026.

item.title: A7A5 stablecoin network moved $179 billion. FinCEN wants US banks and crypto firms out
item.description: A Treasury proposal would bar about 347,926 US financial institutions, crypto exchanges included, from moving money for the Russia-linked A7 network's front companies. Public comments close November 4, 2026.

item.title: What is staking? How proof-of-stake rewards work and how you can lose money
item.description: Staking means locking tokens to help run a proof-of-stake blockchain, in return for rewards paid in that token. The stake is collateral: validators that go offline lose a little, and on Ethereum those that break the rules can be slashed.

item.title: What is Chainlink? How DeFi gets its prices, plus CCIP and LINK staking
item.description: Smart contracts cannot see the outside world, so lending apps rely on oracles like Chainlink to tell them what ether is worth. Chainlink also moves tokens between chains through CCIP, and LINK pays and backs the node operators who do the work.

item.title: What is Ethereum? How the global computer works, what ETH does and the risks
item.description: Ethereum is a public blockchain that runs programs called smart contracts, and ether (ETH) is the coin that pays for using it and secures it through staking. It launched in July 2015, switched from mining to proof of stake on September 15, 2022, and ETH traded near $2,267 as of November 2, 2026.

item.title: What is MEV? How sandwich bots profit from your swap, and how to cut the risk
item.description: MEV, or maximal extractable value, is the profit made by choosing which transactions go into a block and in what order. Some of it keeps prices in line across exchanges. Sandwich attacks take it straight out of ordinary traders' swaps.

item.title: What is TRON? How the chain holding $92.6 billion of USDT really works
item.description: TRON is the blockchain where more of Tether's USDT lives than anywhere else: about $92.6 billion on November 2, 2026, per DefiLlama. Here is how its energy and bandwidth fees work, and why 27 elected block makers decide the rules.

item.title: Arbitrum vote could unfreeze Stylus Rust contracts, but each needs an audit and sign-off
item.description: New Stylus contracts on Arbitrum have been frozen since October 2 over fears of AI-assisted attacks. A DAO poll closing November 5 weighs a way back: every new program would need an auditor's pass and an Arbitrum Foundation signature.

item.title: Send USDC on 12 blockchains, get dollars: OnePay adds Stripe-powered checking deposits
item.description: Since October 30, 2026, select US OnePay customers can send USDC from an outside wallet straight into OnePay Checking. Stripe's Bridge converts it to dollars with no conversion fee at launch, but the coins are not FDIC insured on the way in.

item.title: What is the XRP Ledger? How XRP works with no mining, and what Ripple holds
item.description: The XRP Ledger has run since 2012 and settles a new ledger every 4 to 6 seconds without mining. XRP is its coin, Ripple is a company that does not own it but reported holding 37.66 billion XRP at midyear, and RLUSD is Ripple's stablecoin on it.

item.title: Kenya's crypto grace period ends November 4: KSh 25 million fines for unlicensed firms
item.description: Crypto firms already serving Kenya had one year to get licensed under the new VASP Act, and that year ends Wednesday. From November 4, 2026, a company operating without a license risks a fine of up to KSh 25 million.

item.title: Token unlocks November 2 to 8: $1.05 billion due, led by HYPE, and Kite's float jumps 27%
item.description: Five scheduled unlocks this week add up to about $1.05 billion at November 2 prices, according to CoinGecko's calendars. Hyperliquid's HYPE is almost 80% of the dollar total, but Kite's KITE release is the biggest relative to what already trades.

item.title: What is BNB Chain? Three chains, 21 block makers and 0.45-second blocks
item.description: BNB Chain is three blockchains that all run on BNB: BNB Smart Chain (BSC) for apps, the cheaper layer 2 opBNB and the storage network Greenfield. Its speed comes from a small club: just 21 validators make BSC's blocks at any one time.

item.title: Circle and ACI want banks to settle in USDC on rails they already run. First: Colombia
item.description: ACI Worldwide, which built the core of Colombia's Bre-B instant payment system, will plug Circle's USDC into its payments platform for a Colombian pilot. The two companies gave no volumes, no bank names and no launch date.

item.title: BNB just burned $1.2 billion of itself. Why is 100 million still years away?
item.description: The 37th quarterly auto-burn destroyed 1,646,196 BNB on October 19, the most coins of any burn this year. Supply is now 131.5 million BNB, still 31.5 million above the long-term target.

item.title: bStocks, a Binance affiliate's stock tokens, jumps 53% to $1.31 billion and No. 1
item.description: bStocks, issued on BNB Chain by a Binance group affiliate, is now the largest tokenized stock platform. By our math it added more value in 30 days than the whole $3.58 billion market did, because the rest of the market shrank.

item.title: Zcash NU7 makes blocks 3x faster around November 5. Old nodes will split off
item.description: Zcash's NU7 hard fork activates at block 3,543,405, expected around November 5, 2026. It cuts block time from 75 to 25 seconds without changing supply, sends 60% of fees to a reserve and invalidates version 4 transactions. Nodes that do not upgrade split off.

item.title: How stolen crypto is traced and frozen, and why thieves dump stablecoins fast
item.description: Every blockchain transfer is public, so investigators can follow stolen funds hop by hop. Money can be stopped in two places: stablecoin issuers like Tether and Circle can freeze tokens on-chain, and exchanges can lock accounts when stolen funds arrive.

item.title: Crypto travel rule explained: what exchanges must send with your transfer
item.description: The travel rule requires crypto exchanges and other providers to send the sender's and recipient's details along with a transfer, as banks do with wires. In the EU it applies to every crypto transfer regardless of amount, and 83% of jurisdictions surveyed by the FATF have passed travel rule laws.

item.title: Dubai VARA crypto rules explained: who needs a license and what it covers
item.description: In Dubai, crypto businesses need a license from the Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA), which covers the emirate's mainland and free zones except the DIFC. VARA licenses seven activities, from exchanges to custody, and regulates token issuance and crypto marketing.

item.title: Kalshi prices a Democratic sweep at a record 70%. Did a fake pollster move the odds?
item.description: Two days before the November 3 vote, Kalshi's market priced Democrats winning both chambers at 70%, up more than 9 points in a month. Ten days earlier, Kalshi had to explain why a fabricated pollster barely moved its election markets.

item.title: Stablecoins explained: USDT vs. USDC, the two coins that hold 87% of the market
item.description: Stablecoins are tokens built to stay worth $1, backed by reserves such as cash and short-term US government debt. As of November 2, 2026, Tether's USDT ($178.48 billion) and Circle's USDC ($70.68 billion) made up about 87% of a $285.89 billion market, per rwa.xyz.

item.title: What is Sui? The object-based blockchain that says it settles in 390 ms
item.description: Sui is a layer-1 blockchain from Mysten Labs, founded by former Meta engineers, that launched in May 2023. It stores everything as objects with clear owners, runs smart contracts in Move and, by Sui's own figure, settles transactions in roughly 390 milliseconds. SUI has a 10 billion total supply.

item.title: Copy trading explained: how it works, what lead traders take and why results differ
item.description: Copy trading lets you automatically mirror another trader's positions on an exchange, in return for a share of any profit. Your results can differ from theirs because of order size, slippage and timing, and regulators warn it can encourage herd behavior and frequent trading.

item.title: Seed phrase and hardware wallet safety: the words that guard your crypto
item.description: Your seed phrase is the master key to your wallet: anyone who sees it can take everything, and if you lose it, nobody can restore it. A hardware wallet keeps keys offline, but only if the phrase stays offline too and the device is genuine.

item.title: What is DeepSea (desea.io)? The onchain app that labels wallets and tracks flows
item.description: DeepSea (desea.io) is a web app that labels crypto wallets and tracks what smart money, influencers, whales, exchanges and hackers do onchain. It is run by DeepTek Ltd, and its own terms say the data is information only, not financial advice.

item.title: Japan crypto rules explained: FSA registration, 95% cold storage and 2x leverage
item.description: Crypto exchanges in Japan must register with the Financial Services Agency under the Payment Services Act, keep at least 95% of customer coins offline, and cap retail leverage at 2x. A 2026 government bill would revise the rules again, borrowing from securities law.
